issues.where: Region 5, sun, clouds and air above the left field
issues.what: The white sun is larger and higher, with conspicuous evenly spaced rays across the sky and a fan of light over the field. In a, the sun is lower and veiled by broken clouds, and the warm haze spreads through the field in soft, irregular layers.
issues.fix: Lower the sun by roughly 30 pixels in the comparison frame, shrink the clipped white core, restore the broken cloud bank and replace the radial rays with diffuse, uneven amber haze.

issues.where: Regions 6 and 7, open field through the skyline
issues.what: The visible field has larger, more front-facing, saturated yellow heads and sharp olive foliage, then ends abruptly in a flat dark band and low clumps. The target has a denser receding layer of smaller, more varied rim-lit heads and broad, overlapping wooded ridges with haze between them.
issues.fix: Increase the density and angle variation of distant heads, soften and desaturate the field with distance, and replace the flat dark strip with layered, rolling treelines and low haze.

issues.where: Region 1, head of the central foreground sunflower
issues.what: The bloom is smaller and rounder, with shorter, more saturated and less distinctly layered petals. In a it fills more of the frame and has a darker, slightly oblique disk with long, thin petals glowing mainly along the left edge.
issues.fix: Enlarge the main bloom at its existing anchor, make the disk slightly more oblique and dark, and lengthen and separate the softly amber-lit petals.

issues.where: Regions 2 and 3, central stalk and front-facing leaves
issues.what: The stalk reads as a straight bright stripe rather than a stem with individually resolved backlit hairs and branching petioles. The broad leaves make a heavier silhouette, with yellow-green patches and less readable vein, serration and curl detail than the darker target leaves.
issues.fix: Break up the stem highlight into fine warm hairs, restore the arcing petioles, and give the leaves narrower, irregular silhouettes with darker faces, finely resolved veins and thinner rim light.

issues.where: Foreground grass and soil around and to the right of the main plant
issues.what: The grass reads as a fairly uniform carpet with large ochre clumps and a conspicuously bright strip of exposed soil. In a, the verge is darker and more mottled, with smaller scattered grass glints and less exposed soil.
issues.fix: Break up the repeated grass texture, mute and narrow the ochre strip, and retain small irregular highlights in the cooler, darker ground without altering the intended second plant or its shadow.
